correctness.rationale: The geometric double-six universe is reconstructed exhaustively from 27 classical exceptional divisor classes, then independently from the Weyl orbit of a standard double-six. Exact full-group enumeration finds 51,840 elements, all 25 conjugacy classes and 24 double-six cycle spectra. Only the two order-four classes of sizes 1,620 and 3,240 collide, and their line counts and geometric Picard traces/ranks are verified by exact integer/rational computations. The all-field inference uses the standard Weyl action on lines and a published finite-field realization theorem. The standalone certificate and checking program were run and cross-checked under distinct hash seeds.

originality.rationale: The exact near-injectivity of double-six Galois splitting, its unique order-four collision and its distinction by one rational-line count are not stated in the examined primary literature or matching published mathematical records. General Frobenius class lists, realization theorems and double-six incidence-lattice calculations do not supply this particular inverse spectral comparison without the new 36-point permutation computation. A prior construction using line/tritangent extension counts does not logically imply the double-six near-rigidity assertion.

value.rationale: Galois descent of double-sixes is a natural arithmetic invariant of cubic surfaces and relates to rational contractions and line geometry. The exact 24-of-25 near-rigidity and the sole sharp failure exhibit two actually realized cubic-surface types with identical complete double-six zeta functions but different arithmetic Picard ranks, rational-line counts and surface point counts. Adding one simple geometric count repairs that obstruction. This is a motivated natural complete classification and boundary, rather than a field-specific census or mere recomputation of a Weyl class list.
